proposals.evidence: DEDR 1514 directly gives Kodagu tittï, Kolami kis, Malto cicu and Toda tït fire. Badaga kiccə is supported indirectly by the article’s explicit identification of Toda kic as a Badaga loan; this proposal is for the Badaga source form, not for the borrowed Toda song word. Survey titta, kiss, cicadu and tīttə preserve their endings and transcriptions. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5259 documents Malayalam vayaṟu and Toda pīṟ belly, along with Tamil vayiṟu and the wider vac-Vṯ family. Survey vayarə and pir correspond directly. Ravula bairu/bārə are comparative extensions labelled look-alikes in the source; their initial voicing and contraction remain visible for review. The number474 in the annotation is the page, not the two numeral article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2146 gives Gondi koṛvonj/koṛvos and koduvasaka fat, and Toda kwaḷp fat. Survey Gondi koronj/kodovōs and Toda koɻəppə retain their medial consonant and vowel differences. Source cognacy identifies the family; these remain comparative correspondences rather than literal dictionary spellings. The questioned Kota comparison is excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR497 directly gives Kannada ele/ela, Kota el, Toda es̱ and Tulu irè/ele leaf. Survey yele, ēlu, ers and ira preserve the initial glide, final-vowel and Toda sibilant transcription differences; full article and source cognacy support the same leaf family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3633 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam nākku and Toda nōf tongue; survey nākkə/nākə and nōf preserve their spellings. Betta Kurumba nelgi is a comparative extension toward the nālage/nālige series documented in Kannada, explicitly only a look-alike in the source. This does not treat the Betta form as a literal DEDR attestation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
